occurrences.quote: there is a fundamental factual error in the claim itself: Ebbets Field was a baseball stadium, not an NFL venue. No NFL team has ever played home games at Ebbets Field. Therefore, the claim's premise is false.
Did any NFL team ever play home games at Ebbets Field in Brooklyn?
Which footballer played his entire career for the Brooklyn Dodgers NFL team (1930-1943), and is Jason Pinkston confirmed to be his cousin?

Jason Pinkston | Jason R. Pinkston (born September 5, 1987) is a former American football offensive guard, who played his entire career for the Cleveland Browns of the National Football League (NFL).  He is also the cousin of Todd Pinkston, a former NFL wide receiver.

the provided passages contain no information about: 1. **Any specific footballer** who played for the Brooklyn Dodgers NFL team 2. **Jason Pinkston** or any member of the Pinkston family 3. **Any family relationships** between NFL players and Jason Pinkston

Carl Erskine | Carl Daniel Erskine (born December 13, 1926) is a former right-handed starting pitcher in Major League Baseball who played his entire career for the Brooklyn and Los Angeles Dodgers from 1948 through 1959.
Johnny Kucks | John Charles Kucks (July 27, 1933 – October 31, 2013) was a pitcher for the New York Yankees and Kansas City Athletics in Major League Baseball.
Jason Hanson | Jason Hanson (born June 17, 1970) is a retired football placekicker who spent his entire 21-year career playing for the Detroit Lions of the National Football League.

Emerson Boozer | Emerson Boozer (born July 4, 1943) is a former running back in the American Football League (AFL) and in the National Football League (NFL).  In the last year of separate drafts by the AFL and the NFL, Boozer signed with the AFL's New York Jets, rather than with an NFL team.  He played his entire professional career with the Jets.
Jason Snelling | Jason Michael Snelling (born December 29, 1983) is a former American football running back.  He played his entire career with the Atlanta Falcons of the National Football League.

Steve Sader | Stephen J. J. Sader was a professional football player for the Philadelphia Eagles of the National Football League.  However, he was also a member of the "Steagles", a team that was the result of a temporary merger between the Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers due to the league-wide manning shortages in 1943 brought on by World War II.

edges.label: follow_up
edges.evidence: The claim contains a factual impossibility that makes it impossible to verify. Ebbets Field was a baseball stadium in Brooklyn, New York, that was the home of the Brooklyn Dodgers (MLB) from 1913 to 1957. No NFL team has ever played their home games at Ebbets Field.

edges.label: correction
edges.evidence: From passage [1]: "Ebbets Field was a Major League Baseball stadium... also home to three National Football League teams in the 1920s." From passage [2]: "The Brooklyn Dodgers were an American football team that played in the National Football League from 1930 to 1943... The team played its home games at Ebbets Field."
